title: Actual causes
description: Halpern and Pearl's actual causation on the rock-throwing story: is Suzy's throw a cause of the bottle shattering, although Billy's rock would have hit it otherwise (Sigma-2-complete for single-variable causes)? The abstraction guesses a witness, variables held at chosen values under which flipping the cause changes the effect; the check tries to change the effect with the cause in place, by applying part of the witness and freezing other variables. Set the constant cause to bt: no solution, Billy's throw is not a cause.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The variables of the story and the effect. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: model
fragments.description: The structural equations, for any scenario; used by solver A and by solver C.
fragments.text:
% The causal model. val(S,V): variable V is 1 in scenario S.
% set(S,V,B): scenario S holds V at the value B by an intervention; the equation of a
% held variable is switched off.
held(S,V) :- set(S,V,_).
val(S,V)  :- set(S,V,1).
% Suzy throws; Billy throws.
val(S,st) :- scenario(S), not held(S,st).
val(S,bt) :- scenario(S), not held(S,bt).
% Suzy's rock hits if she throws; Billy's hits if he throws and hers did not hit.
val(S,sh) :- scenario(S), not held(S,sh), val(S,st).
val(S,bh) :- scenario(S), not held(S,bh), val(S,bt), not val(S,sh).
% The bottle shatters if a rock hits it.
val(S,bs) :- scenario(S), not held(S,bs), val(S,sh).
val(S,bs) :- scenario(S), not held(S,bs), val(S,bh).
% The actual world: no interventions.
scenario(actual).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): witnesses that pass condition (a).
fragments.text:
% A candidate witness: a set W of variables other than the cause (inw/1), each held at
% a value (wval(V) means 1).
{ inw(V) } :- var(V), V != cause.
{ wval(V) } :- inw(V).
% Condition (a): give the cause the other value and hold W; the effect changes.
scenario(flip).
set(flip,cause,0) :- val(actual,cause).
set(flip,cause,1) :- not val(actual,cause).
set(flip,V,1) :- inw(V), wval(V).
set(flip,V,0) :- inw(V), not wval(V).
:- effect(E), val(actual,E), val(flip,E).
:- effect(E), not val(actual,E), not val(flip,E).
#show.
#show hold(V,1) : inw(V), wval(V).
#show hold(V,0) : inw(V), not wval(V).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the witness set and its values.
fragments.text:
glue(inw(V))  :- var(V), V != cause.
glue(wval(V)) :- var(V), V != cause.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a violation of condition (b) (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample to condition (b): the cause keeps its actual value, some variables
% of W are held at the witness values (part/1), some other variables are frozen at
% their actual values (frozen/1), and the effect changes all the same.
scenario(test).
set(test,cause,1) :- val(actual,cause).
set(test,cause,0) :- not val(actual,cause).
{ part(V) } :- inw(V).
set(test,V,1) :- part(V), wval(V).
set(test,V,0) :- part(V), not wval(V).
{ frozen(V) } :- var(V), V != cause, not inw(V).
set(test,V,1) :- frozen(V), val(actual,V).
set(test,V,0) :- frozen(V), not val(actual,V).
:- effect(E), val(actual,E), val(test,E).
:- effect(E), not val(actual,E), not val(test,E).
#show part/1.
#show frozen/1.

% The same test applies to every witness that still holds the variables in part/1 at
% the same values and still leaves the frozen variables out of W.
relevant(inw(V))  :- part(V).
relevant(wval(V)) :- part(V).
relevant(inw(V))  :- frozen(V).

fragments.name: check_small
fragments.description: The check of the variant smallest: a counterexample that holds and freezes as few variables as possible, so the clause is short.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample to condition (b): the cause keeps its actual value, some variables
% of W are held at the witness values (part/1), some other variables are frozen at
% their actual values (frozen/1), and the effect changes all the same.
scenario(test).
set(test,cause,1) :- val(actual,cause).
set(test,cause,0) :- not val(actual,cause).
{ part(V) } :- inw(V).
set(test,V,1) :- part(V), wval(V).
set(test,V,0) :- part(V), not wval(V).
{ frozen(V) } :- var(V), V != cause, not inw(V).
set(test,V,1) :- frozen(V), val(actual,V).
set(test,V,0) :- frozen(V), not val(actual,V).
:- effect(E), val(actual,E), val(test,E).
:- effect(E), not val(actual,E), not val(test,E).
#show part/1.
#show frozen/1.
% The smallest refinement: as few held and frozen variables as possible (the loop asks
% for an optimal counterexample).
#minimize { 1,p,V : part(V); 1,f,V : frozen(V) }.

% The same test applies to every witness that still holds the variables in part/1 at
% the same values and still leaves the frozen variables out of W.
relevant(inw(V))  :- part(V).
relevant(wval(V)) :- part(V).
relevant(inw(V))  :- frozen(V).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + model + abstraction
solver C = shared + model + check       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% Suzy and Billy both throw a rock at a bottle. Suzy's rock gets there first.
% st, bt: Suzy / Billy throws.  sh, bh: Suzy's / Billy's rock hits.  bs: the bottle shatters.
var(st;bt;sh;bh;bs).
% The effect to be explained.
effect(bs).

% The same story, with Billy's throw as the candidate cause: it is not a cause.
var(st;bt;sh;bh;bs).
effect(bs).

% Is Suzy's throw a cause of Billy's rock not hitting?
var(st;bt;sh;bh;bs).
effect(bh).

% Is the bottle shattering a cause of Billy's rock not hitting? No: whatever is held, the
% miss does not depend on the bottle.
var(st;bt;sh;bh;bs).
effect(bh).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + model + abstraction
solver C = shared + model + check       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: each refuted candidate is ruled out on its own.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + model + abstraction
solver C = shared + model + check       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Shape 2: explicit solves of A; each solution is blocked by A.add.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + model + abstraction
solver C = shared + model + check       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three counterexamples per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + model + abstraction
solver C = shared + model + check       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The smallest refinement: an optimal counterexample (check_small minimises the
# atoms that relevant/1 blames), so its clause is as short as possible.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

library.summary: Halpern-Pearl actual causation on the rock-throwing story: witnesses for Suzy's throw being a cause (cause = st, 4 solutions; cause = bt, none).
